first.rationale: Two of three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) map directly to durable, well-supported findings (memory_31, memory_86) with no flagged data-quality issues, and improving onboarding/activation supports sustainable qualified revenue without the retention-quality risk of chasing price-sensitive share against a competitor's aggressive entry pricing. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitive threat, but that memory explicitly flags a mid-test cohort redefinition that pooled two segments, so its acquisition/revenue lift figures are suspect until verified against the original record; it also risks attracting low-LTV price-shoppers rather than sustainable qualified revenue, which is the stated objective. I'm verifying memory_73 to check whether the pooling issue invalidates or merely qualifies its conclusion, and memory_86 to confirm it's a distinct, corroborating result rather than a restatement of memory_31 under a different framing, since both claim onboarding-related lifts and I want independent support before committing the week's only experiment slot. Given only one experiment fits this week and two problems (activation, onboarding) are more actionable with cleaner evidence than the pricing response, I'm prioritizing onboarding simplification at a standard (not broad) scale to gather fresh confirmatory data under current conditions before considering a larger rollout or pivoting to pricing/referral levers next cycle.
